rules: 1. Imports: add useLocation and useParams to the react-router-dom import, and import getRenamedFromEntityRef from '../TechDocsRedirectNotification/TechDocsRenamedNotification'; keep all existing imports.

Former ref: when catalogEntity is undefined, renamedFromEntityRef is undefined (loop guard, NFR-6) and catalogApi.getEntityByFormerRef exists, call it with entityRef; when it resolves an entity and buildTechDocsURL(renamedEntity, viewTechdocLink) gives a base, return { to: base without trailing slashes + (docsPath ? `/${docsPath}` : '') + location.search + location.hash, state: { renamedFromEntityRef: entityKey } }.

7. The effect navigates when the value is set: navigate(value.to, { replace: true }) when value.state is undefined, and navigate(value.to, { replace: true, state: value.state }) otherwise; the checkedEntityRef bookkeeping is unchanged.
8. shouldShowProgress stays (shouldCheckForRedirect && loading) || Boolean(value), so the reader shows progress instead of its not-found state while the redirect happens.

rules: 1. Explain the value is a comma-separated list of entity refs the entity was previously known by; whitespace around items is ignored and empty items are skipped.

2. Explain defaulting: a bare name uses the entity's own kind and namespace, a namespace/name ref uses the entity's own kind; refs with a different kind than the entity, refs that fail to parse and the entity's own ref are ignored; matching is case-insensitive.
3. Show a yaml '# Example:' block with metadata.name new-name and annotation backstage.io/former-refs: old-name, legacy/older-name.

4. Conflict rules: when an entity currently exists with the requested ref, the old ref does not resolve (the live entity wins); when more than one entity declares the same former ref, it resolves to nothing.

5. Permissions: a former ref only resolves to an entity the caller may read; otherwise it behaves as an unknown ref, so the new name is not revealed. Link to the lookup endpoint in api.md (#get-entitiesby-former-namekindnamespacename).

6. Frontend: the catalog entity page and the TechDocs reader redirect an old link to the renamed entity, keep the rest of the path, query string and hash, and show a dismissible notice; only one hop is followed, so list every former ref on the current entity; the index updates the next time the catalog processes the entity after its annotation changes.

2. Body: Added the `backstage.io/former-refs` well-known annotation, which lets an entity list the entity refs it was previously known by, along with the `ANNOTATION_FORMER_REFS` constant and a `getEntityFormerRefs` helper that returns those refs in normalized form.

Body: Added an optional `getEntityByFormerRef` method to `CatalogApi`, implemented by `CatalogClient`, which returns the entity that currently declares a given ref in its `backstage.io/former-refs` annotation, or `undefined` when there is no match. Custom `CatalogApi` implementations do not need to change.
1. Front matter: '@backstage/plugin-catalog-backend': minor

2. Body: The catalog now indexes the entity refs that entities list in the `backstage.io/former-refs` annotation and serves them through a new `GET /entities/by-former-name/:kind/:namespace/:name` endpoint, which returns the entity that currently declares the given former ref. A ref that an existing entity holds, or that more than one entity declares, does not resolve, and callers only receive entities they are allowed to read. This release includes a database migration that adds a table for the index.
